newsitem.title: UK: Bank of England warns on Internet banking risks.
newsitem.headline: Bank of England warns on Internet banking risks.

text.p: The Bank of England on Monday warned potential customers of Internet "banks" that they could run risks unless they are certain that the operation is authorised in the UK.

The Bank said that while widening the choice for customers, Internet banking can mean that it may be difficult to establish the credentials of some firms and it may even be unclear from which country they are operating.
"Compensation arrangements in the event of product failure may be weak or non-existent," the Bank says in its latest Financial Stability Review.

The Bank says anyone considering placing deposits or buying investment products should check to see if the firm is authorised either with the BOE or the Securities and Investments Board which maintains a register of authorised firms.
For financial companies which have no physical presence in the UK, potential investors are advised to check with the relevant regulator in the country concerned.
The Bank said those wishing to get further information can access its web site at http://www.bankofengland.co.uk.
